llm.summary: This is a straightforward Chinese diet-tracking skill that stores user-entered meal data locally, with no evidence of hidden network access, privilege escalation, or deceptive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The script reads and writes only ~/.qclaw/workspace/diet.json, which is proportionate for a local tracker, though users should understand this may contain personal health-related entries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency fetch, remote payload retrieval, service registration, or background setup was found in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are user-directed CLI examples for adding records and viewing reports, with no role changes, prompt overrides, hidden commands, or automatic execution.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is limited to a disclosed local JSON file and uses normal user privileges; there is no privilege escalation, scheduled task, tool wrapping, or cross-session agent behavior, but no deletion or retention controls are documented.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact coherently implements a local diet tracker for foods, calories, categories, notes, daily targets, and reports; the SKILL.md also advertises nutrition macro analysis, but the inspected script does not implement carb/protein/fat tracking.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use this if you are comfortable with a Chinese-language CLI saving meal, calorie, category, note, and target data locally at ~/.qclaw/workspace/diet.json. On shared systems, protect or remove that file when needed because food logs can be sensitive personal data.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Local JSON read/write is necessary for the stated tracking function and the path is disclosed; I found no evidence of broader file access, so this is guidance rather than a Review-level concern.
[SQP-3] expected: The SKILL.md is Chinese-only and the title explicitly frames it as a Chinese diet tracker; this is a locale limitation, not evidence of unsafe behavior.
[SQP-3] expected: The script's CLI text and output are Chinese-only, consistent with the skill's stated audience and not a security concern.
[SQP-2] expected: The persistence of diet entries is purpose-aligned and the local file path is disclosed, but a clearer privacy notice and delete/export controls would be useful.
